condition.label: degenerative meniscal lesion
condition.distinctions: Degenerative lesion differs from acute traumatic, bucket-handle/root/displaced tears and repaired meniscus.

scope.population: Middle-aged adults with symptomatic degenerative meniscal lesions; ESCAPE 45–70.
scope.stage: Nonlocked degenerative tear with conservative treatment; acute displaced tears distinct.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonsurgical initial care; partial meniscectomy, repair and reconstruction require different stage-specific management.
scope.exclusions: Locked knee, acute surgical trauma, cruciate instability, KL 4 andBMI>35 excluded from ESCAPE; exclusions are not contraindications.
scope.uncertainty: Research extraction only; no universal safe dose, clearance or diagnosis inferred.

sources.population: Age 45–70, MRI-confirmed symptomatic degenerative tears; locked knee, acute-surgery trauma, cruciate instability, KL 4, BMI>35 excluded.
sources.comparator: Physical therapy vs arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
sources.coInterventions: Surgery: home exercise instructions; PT if delayed recovery. PT: extra sessions/delayed surgery if persistent symptoms.
sources.outcomes: IKDC improvement 25.1 PT vs 29.6 surgery; 5-year crude MD 3.5 (95%CI 0.7, 6.3)within 11-point noninferiority margin; similar OA progression. PT 32.1%delayed surgery.
sources.uncertainty: Crossover, unblinded, loss to follow-up, noninvasive cointerventions not registered. Source narrative crossover timing inconsistent; do not infer universal success.
sources.harms: 5-year report refers earlier 2-year adverse-event report; 17additional operations(5 surgery, 12 PT); not exercise-harm equivalence.
sources.limitations: Crossover, unblinded, loss to follow-up, noninvasive cointerventions not registered. Source narrative crossover timing inconsistent; do not infer universal success.

protocol.execution: Incremental exercise program; exact tasks, coordination and strength details not supplied in main report; supplement not retrieved.
protocol.frequency: 2/week implied by 16 in 8 weeks; actual spacing not prescribed in main report.
protocol.progression: Incremental program; detailed load/ROM/sets not available in inspected main report.
protocol.stoppingRules: Persistent pain/function/mechanical symptoms prompted review, extra PT or surgeon discussion; no numeric rule.

sources.population: Separate acute traumatic tears, degenerative lesions and postoperative procedures.
sources.comparator: Nonoperative vs surgery; multiple rehab strategies.
sources.coInterventions: Home exercise added to supervised therapy; manual/ROM options.
sources.outcomes: Degenerative lesions: PT-first GRADEA; progressive knee/hip strength and neuromuscular/ROM training GRADEB. No direct supervised-vs-home comparison(GRADED).
sources.uncertainty: Many criteria based on consensus; no one optimal exercise dose; postrepair restrictions cannot be transferred to untreated degenerative lesions.
sources.harms: No pooled harms rate. Persistent symptoms/effusion/instability/mechanical symptoms merit surgical referral.
sources.limitations: Many criteria based on consensus; no one optimal exercise dose; postrepair restrictions cannot be transferred to untreated degenerative lesions.

protocol.execution: Progressive knee/hip strengthening, ROM, neuromuscular training.
protocol.dose: not reported as a standard sets/reps/load prescription
protocol.frequency: not reported as a standard frequency
protocol.supervision: Supervised PT with home exercise suggested; supervised-vs-home untested.
protocol.progression: Criterion-based assessment of symptoms, effusion, ROM, strength/control; consider healing time.
protocol.stoppingRules: Refer persistent pain, recurring effusion/functional instability/mechanical symptoms; clinical assessment required.

findings.statement: Consensus advises referral for persistent pain, recurring stiffness/effusion, functional instability or mechanical symptoms; return is criterion-based with knee function and healing considerations.

exerciseMappings.matchRationale: Catalog squats/leg-press cannot be matched to an unspecified incremental program. Preserve a protocol-retrieval candidate, not a new generic exercise or approval of every squat.

proposedRules.statement: Retain the documented incremental strengthening program as a research candidate after exact task retrieval; ordinary exercise selection should be individualized with symptom review.

gaps: Researcher appraisal, not formal GRADE: moderate-to-high confidence in managed PT-first strategy for nonlocked degenerative lesions; low confidence in a specific app exercise identity/dose.
ESCAPE exercise supplement not retrieved; actual individual sets/reps/load and progression unresolved.
No deep-squat/twisting ban or universal 90-degree cap justified for every untreated degenerative lesion.
Postrepair consensus restrictions encountered during search are procedure-specific and not transferred to this condition.
Delayed surgery 32% means response is not guaranteed; currentness check included 2025consensus.
Independent clinical review absent; doses are reported study protocols, not app prescriptions.
No universal contraindication follows from trial exclusion or another exercise showing benefit. No generic five-second progression or stretch strength-set credit.
